This interactive dashboard provides a centralized view of business tax data across Broward County. It is designed to support transparency, operational insight, and strategic planning by visualizing key metrics. You can filter using different attributes and metrics will update based upon the business being located inside or outside Broward County.

The dashboard integrates data maintained by the Records, Taxes, and Treasury Division and is supported by Broward County GIS, which ensures system performance through ArcGIS Enterprise services.

attributes.description:
Important notes about this data:
  • Receipts are added/updated from the Local Business Tax Information report provided by the Lee County Tax Collector here: https://lee.county-taxes.com/public/reports/business_tax.
  • A single business may have multiple receipts.
  • This is not a comprehensive list of all businesses that have ever existed in Lee County. Most businesses closed prior to the 2022 tax year have been removed.
  • Mobile businesses operating in Lee County but based elsewhere are included in this data and their points are placed off the coast of Lee County in the Gulf of Mexico. Use the "Business Address in County?" field to filter these businesses.
  • A business tax account may still have an "Account Status" of "ACTIVE" after going out of business. Some businesses may not submit an out of business affidavit; these are typically flagged by the Tax Collector as "CLOSED" after 2 or more years. Because of this, the "Business Closed Date" may not accurately reflect when the business closed, but rather when the account was closed.
  • The "Common Name" field has been added to store a commonly used or colloquial version of the business name. This typically involves stripping things like "INC" or "LLC" or "STORE #13390" from the business name. This field can be for labeling and searching.
"Individuals or business entities choosing to start a business, or who have an established business from another county, will need to obtain a Business Tax Account prior to doing business in Lee County.

While exemptions may apply, a Business Tax Application still needs to be submitted along with the affidavit. The Business Tax Affidavit will provide applicable exemptions and must be submitted with your application.

Businesses that begin offering goods or services from April 1 thru September 30 will pay a prorated fee.

All business tax receipts expire September 30 of each year and can be renewed after July 1. BT Express is our online service for initial applications, renewals, or any changes to name, address, ownership, or status of your business." - Lee County Tax Collector

For more information, please visit https://www.leetc.com/businesses

attributes.description:
Overview

This feature service provides comprehensive tax-related business information for local businesses within Broward County as well as businesses located outside Broward County. It consolidates data from two primary feature layers that represent business tax databases, supporting up-to-date business tax tracking and management.

Feature Layers
  • Local Business Tax Database: This layer contains detailed business tax records for local Broward County businesses, including business names, owner information, addresses, and tax payment details. The dataset features historical and current tax data updated as of late 2024, providing valuable insights into business activities, tax categories, and business start dates within the county.

attributes.description:
Overview

This feature service provides detailed information about businesses primarily located in Broward County and includes a separate dataset for businesses located outside Broward County. It is designed to support tax administration and business analysis by capturing a comprehensive set of business details, including business names, ownership, addresses, categories, and start dates.

Feature Layers
  • Local Business Tax Database: This layer contains detailed records of businesses registered for local tax purposes within Broward County. It includes information such as business and DBA names, owner names, physical and mailing addresses, business categories, occupation descriptions, and official start dates. The data also incorporates district and perimeter information relevant to administrative boundaries and tax districts, along with website details and receipt numbers for transactions.
  • Non-Broward Business Address: This complementary layer provides similar information for businesses outside Broward County. It captures essential business and mailing address data, categories, and start dates to support broader regional business analyses and address verification processes.
Geographic Coverage

The datasets focus on Broward County, Florida for the local business tax layer, while also including business address information for non-Broward locations presumably relevant for cross-jurisdictional or comparative purposes.

Use Cases
  • Support for local government tax collection and compliance efforts.
  • Business licensing and regulatory administration.
  • Economic development analysis and business demographic studies.
  • Provision of business address validation and categorization services for public and private sector users.

attributes.description: Through the Supermarket Tax Exemption Act of 2000, the District waives certain taxes and fees to grocery stores that locate in specific neighborhoods. The incentive encourages development and investment in areas lacking access to groceries and fresh food. Qualifying supermarkets may be eligible to receive one or more of the following benefits for up to 10 years after development or renovation: real property tax exemption; business license fee exemption; personal property tax exemption; sales and use tax exemption on building materials necessary for construction when prior notification is sent to the District of Columbia. Confirm the latest qualification requirements by visiting dmped.dc.gov under business initiatives. Learn more about the Supermarket Tax Incentive in the Code for the District of Columbia: https://code.dccouncil.gov/us/dc/council/code/titles/47/chapters/38.

attributes.description:
A business may qualify for the program if it is located inside the Capital beltway (the area between the District of Columbia's border and the I-495 Beltway), or within a quarter-mile of rail transit stations.

 

This website provides a map that allows users to determine if a location meets the above criteria. It also allows users to export the map extent to PDF.

 

For more information about the program (including additional eligibility criteria), and how to apply, please visit the EDC's additional tax incentives page.
